sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: LARGE UPR TROUGH WILL CONTINUE TO DEEPEN OVER THE WRN HALF OF THE COUNTRY ON THURSDAY. EMBEDDED WITHIN THE LARGER SCALE TROUGH...A POTENT MID-LVL WAVE WILL TRAVEL FROM THE GRT BASIN REGION EARLY THURSDAY INTO THE NRN/CNTRL PLAINS BY NIGHTFALL. AT THE SFC...A FRONT DECELERATING ACROSS THE DKTS...NW KS AND THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS WILL RESUME A ESE TRANSLATION BY THURSDAY NIGHT AS A DOMINANT SFC LOW MIGRATES TOWARD THE UPR MS VLY. PORTIONS OF THIS FRONT WILL BE THE FOCUS FOR SVR TSTMS THURSDAY AFTN/NIGHT ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE UPR MS VLY TO THE CNTRL PLAINS.

sections.title: UPR MS VLY TO THE CNTRL PLAINS
sections.text: LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE OVER THE RIO GRANDE VALLEY/TX HIGH PLAINS WILL BE RAPIDLY TRANSPORTED NWD INTO THE CNTRL PLAINS AND UPR MS VLY BENEATH A STRONG CAP ON THURSDAY. BY LATE AFTN...MID/UPR 50S SFC DEW POINTS WILL BE COMMON ALONG/AHEAD OF THE CDFNT WITH CAPES 1000-1500 J/KG. AS AFOREMENTIONED PV-ANOMOLY SWINGS NEWD FROM THE CNTRL ROCKIES EARLY THURSDAY AFTN...HIGH-BASED TSTMS WILL DEVELOP ACROSS THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS WITH ISOLD DMGG WIND GUSTS/HAIL. MORE ROBUST DEEP MOIST CONVECTION WILL EVOLVE MID-LATE AFTN IN WRN IA AND ERN NEB AND EXPAND SWD INTO AT LEAST NCNTRL/NERN KS AS THE EML MOISTENS/COOLS VIA DEEP-LAYER ASCENT. 50+KT SLY H92/85 FLOW VEERING TO 75+KT SWLY H5 WINDS WILL BOOST EFFECTIVE SHEAR TO OVER 65 KTS AND WILL SUPPORT SUPERCELLS INITIALLY. 0-1KM SRH WILL INCREASE DURING THE LATE AFTN/EARLY EVE OWING TO NOCTURNAL ACCELERATION OF THE LLJ. SFC TEMP/DEW-POINT SPREADS WILL BE SOMEWHAT HIGH AT INITIATION...BUT WILL LOWER COINCIDENT WITH INCREASE IN LOW-LEVEL SHEAR. THUS...ISOLD TORNADOES WILL BE POSSIBLE...PRIMARILY WITH LONGER-LIVED DISCRETE STORMS. OTHERWISE...MAGNITUDE OF LAPSE RATES/SHEAR WILL SUPPORT VERY LARGE HAIL AND SPORADIC DMGG WIND GUSTS. sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A BROAD...SLOW MOVING UPPER TROUGH COVERS MOST OF THE COUNTRY...WEST OF THE ROCKIES...WITH A SERIES OF UPPER LEVEL IMPULSES ROTATING CYCLONICALLY THROUGH THIS SYSTEM. WV IMAGERY SUGGESTS ONE OF THESE IMPULSES...CURRENTLY LOCATED IN SRN CO... WILL SHIFT NEWD INTO KS/NEB THIS AFTERNOON. THIS SHOULD AID STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS DEVELOPING ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE CENTRAL PLAINS/MID MO RIVER VALLEY LATE THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING. A SURFACE LOW WAS LOCATED WEST OF FSD THIS MORNING...WITH COLD FRONT TRAILING SWWD INTO SWRN KS. HOWEVER...APPROACHING IMPULSE IS LIKELY TO AID IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW SURFACE LOW ALONG FRONT IN NRN/NERN KS LATER THIS AFTERNOON. COLD FRONT AND LOW WILL MOVE ONLY SLIGHTLY EWD THROUGH THE PERIOD DUE TO THE SLOW MOTION OF THE UPPER TROUGH.

sections.title: PORTIONS OF THE CENTRAL PLAINS AND MID MO RIVER VALLEY
sections.text: ALTHOUGH SURFACE LOW PRESSURE OVER THE CENTRAL PLAINS WILL RESULT IN STRONG SLY WINDS AND A SLOW INCREASE IN SURFACE DEWPOINTS INTO THE MID AND UPPER 50S TODAY...GOES PW VALUES ONLY RANGE FROM 3/4 TO 1 INCH FROM THE TX COAST NWD INTO THE SLIGHT RISK AREA. DESPITE WEAK MOISTURE RETURN...SUNNY SKIES AND CONSEQUENT STRONG HEATING WILL LEAD TO STEEPENING LOW/MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES FROM ERN KS NEWD INTO IA. THE COMBINATION OF INCREASING SURFACE DEWPOINTS AND STEEPENING LAPSE RATES SHOULD YIELD MODERATE INSTABILITY BY LATE AFTERNOON EAST OF THE SURFACE LOW/FRONT. WHILE STORMS MAY INITIALLY DEVELOP BEHIND THE FRONT IN KS/NEB AROUND MID AFTERNOON...STRONGER CONVECTION IS MOST LIKELY TO EVOLVE NEAR AND NORTHEAST OF THE SURFACE LOW IN NERN KS/SERN NEB BY 00Z. THIS CONVECTION SHOULD EXPAND INTO IA/MN AS THE FORCING SPREADS NEWD...WITH STORMS ALSO DEVELOPING SWD ALONG THE FRONT INTO SRN KS. WHILE A TORNADO OR TWO IS CERTAINLY POSSIBLE NEAR THE GREATER LOW LEVEL SHEAR NEAR THE SURFACE LOW...THE POOR BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE FAVORS SEVERE HAIL AS THE PRIMARY THREAT. sections.title: 20Z UPDATE
sections.text: ONLY MINOR CHANGES HAVE BEEN MADE TO CATEGORICAL AND PROBABILISTIC OUTLOOK LINES...WHICH ARE GENERALLY REFLECTIVE OF LINGERING UNCERTAINTIES CONCERNING TIMING AND LOCATION OF STRENGTHENING LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR UPWARD VERTICAL MOTION. FAIRLY RAPID DESTABILIZATION IS NOW WELL UNDERWAY ACROSS THE CENTRAL PLAINS AND MIDDLE/LOWER MISSOURI VALLEY NORTHEASTWARD INTO PARTS OF THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY. STRONGEST SURFACE HEATING IS ONGOING IN A NARROW PRE-COLD FRONTAL CORRIDOR ACROSS SOUTH CENTRAL THROUGH NORTHEAST KANSAS...SOUTHEAST NEBRASKA AND NORTHWEST MISSOURI...INTO WESTERN IOWA. THIS IS OCCURRING NEARLY COINCIDENT WITH THE NORTHWARD RETURN OF MID/UPPER 50S SURFACE DEW POINTS...BENEATH WEAK MID-LEVEL COOLING ASSOCIATED WITH THE PASSAGE OF AN INITIAL SHORT WAVE IMPULSE LIFTING TOWARD THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY. IT APPEARS REMAINING INHIBITION COULD WEAKEN SUFFICIENTLY TO ALLOW STORM DEVELOPMENT ACROSS EASTERN NEBRASKA INTO WESTERN IOWA PRIOR TO 30/00Z. IF THIS OCCURS...THE ENVIRONMENT...CHARACTERIZED BY STEEP LAPSE RATES AND MIXED LAYER CAPE AROUND 1000 J/KG...IN THE PRESENCE OF WIND PROFILES WITH STRONG DEEP LAYER SHEAR AND SIZABLE CLOCKWISE CURVED LOW-LEVEL HODOGRAPHS...WILL

sections.title: CNTRL PLAINS
sections.text: TSTMS HAVE FORMED NEAR THE TROUGH WITH A COUPLE OF SUPERCELLS OVER NCNTRL KS AND SERN NEB EARLY THIS EVE. ACCELERATING SLY LLJ WILL CONTINUALLY FEED UNSTABLE PARCELS INTO CNTRL KS WITH THERMODYNAMIC/KINEMATIC SET-UPS FAVORING BACKBUILDING CELLS FOR SVRL HOURS. BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE WILL SURGE TO THE CDFNT THROUGH MID-EVE AND INITIAL HIGH-BASED STORMS WILL ROOT INTO THE IMPROVING INSTABILITY. GIVEN OBSERVED 0-1KM SRH 200-400 M2/S2...A COUPLE OF TORNADOES WILL BE POSSIBLE ACROSS NCNTRL KS...SERN NEB AND WRN IA. OTHERWISE...VERY LARGE HAIL AND DMGG WIND GUSTS CAN BE EXPECTED. TORNADO THREAT WILL DECREASE OVERNIGHT AS THE CDFNT SURGES SE...UNDERCUTTING SFC-BASED STORMS. ELEVATED STORMS WILL CONTINUE TO PRODUCE LARGE HAIL.

sections.title: UPR MS VLY
sections.text: MEANWHILE...AS PV-ANOMALY CONTINUES ENE ACROSS THE CNTRL PLAINS TONIGHT...STORMS WILL INCREASE IN NUMBER/INTENSITY FARTHER NE IN THE UPR MS VLY WHERE INSTABILITY/LLVL SHEAR WILL BE COMPARATIVELY WEAKER. EFFECTIVE DEEP LAYER SHEAR AND STEEP MID-LVL LAPSE RATES WILL SUPPORT A SUPERCELL THREAT WITH PRIMARILY LARGE HAIL. A BRIEF TORNADO CANNOT BE RULED OUT...BUT GIVEN TENDENCY FOR STORMS TO REMAIN WITHIN PRE-FRONTAL TROUGH/FRONT CIRCULATION...THE NUMBER/COMPETITION OF UPDRAFTS MAY EVENTUALLY CONTRIBUTE TO STRENGTHENING COLD POOL GENERATION AND LESSEN RISKS FOR DISCRETE STORMS. ..RACY.. 04/30/2010
